facts.statement: Alaskacephale is a genus of dinosaur.

facts.quote: species: gangloffi

facts.statement: The genus was established by Robert Sullivan in 2006.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Sullivan, 2006

facts.quote: authority: Sullivan, 2006

facts.statement: Alaskacephale belongs to the suborder Pachycephalosauria.
facts.quote: infraordo: Pachycephalosauria

facts.statement: It is classified within the family Pachycephalosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Pachycephalosauridae

facts.statement: Alaskacephale lived during the early Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: early Maastrichtian,

facts.statement: This dinosaur lived in northern Alaska during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now northern Alaska

facts.statement: The only known fossil, a squamosal bone, was discovered in 1999.
facts.quote: The only known specimen, a squamosal bone, was found in 1999 and later described in 2005

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Prince Creek Formation.
facts.quote: found in the Prince Creek Formation

facts.statement: The fossil was unearthed from bluffs on the Colville River in Alaska during a 1999 University of Alaska expedition.
facts.quote: In 1999 during an expedition by the University of Alaska, an isolated pachycephalosaur squamosal was unearthed from bluffs on the bank of the Colville River in North Slope Borough, Alaska

facts.statement: Roland Gangloff and colleagues first described the fossil in 2005.
facts.quote: described in 2005 by Roland Gangloff and colleagues

facts.statement: The genus name combines "Alaska" and the Greek word for "head".
facts.quote: The genus name comes from Alaska, the state the holotype (name-bearing specimen) was found in, and cephale, from the Greek kephale meaning "head"

facts.statement: The species name gangloffi honors Roland Gangloff for his earlier description.
facts.quote: Its species name is in honor of Gangloff, who published the earlier 2005 description

facts.statement: Bony protuberances on the skull confirm it was a pachycephalosaur.
facts.quote: Despite this, the presence of bony protuberances from the skull prove that it was a pachycephalosaur

facts.statement: It is distinguished by two rows of nodules along the squamosal bone.
facts.quote: Alaskacephale is distinguished from other genera by the two rows of nodules found along the squamosal

facts.statement: It was estimated to be about half the size of Pachycephalosaurus or three-quarters the size of Prenocephale.
facts.quote: The dimensions of the holotype suggest that A. gangloffi was about half the size of Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis or three-quarters the size of Prenocephale

facts.statement: The reference species Sphaerotholus measured 1.5 meters long and weighed 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: The latter measured 1.5 m long and 10 kg in weight

facts.statement: Alaskacephale is considered one of the smaller known pachycephalosaurs.
facts.quote: This would make Alaskacephale one of the smaller known pachycephalosaurs

facts.statement: No postcranial fossils of Alaskacephale have been discovered.
facts.quote: No postcranial fossils belonging to Alaskacephale have been found

facts.statement: Its neck was slender, U-shaped, and held in a curved posture.
facts.quote: The neck was slender and U-shaped, and held in a curved posture, attaching at the occipital condyle on the back of the skull

facts.statement: Its arms were lightly built and ended in a hand with five fingers.
facts.quote: Its arms were lightly-built and slender ending in a hand with five fingers

facts.statement: Its feet had three toes, with the middle toe being the longest and all having claws.
facts.quote: The limbs terminated in a pes with three toes, the middle being the longest, all of which had unguals

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a skull fragment including a nearly complete left squamosal, parts of the supraorbital, quadrate, and postorbital.
facts.quote: The only known specimen consists of a skull fragment containing a nearly complete left squamosal, much of the left posterior supraorbital, a fragment of the quadrate, and sections of the postorbital

facts.statement: The nodes have polygonal bases with distinct grooves, unlike the rounded nodules of Pachycephalosaurus.
facts.quote: All of these nodes have polygonal bases, unlike the rounded nodules in Pachycephalosaurus, with distinct grooves separating them

facts.statement: The squamosal features twelve nodes, with the largest located at the base of the parietal.
facts.quote: The squamosal has twelve of these nodes, the largest of which is at the base of the parietal

facts.statement: The preserved dome has a maximum thickness of 4.05 centimeters.
facts.quote: Part of the dome is preserved, with the thickest point being 4.05 cm thick

facts.statement: The nuchal shelf at the back of the skull is only 1.50 centimeters thick.
facts.quote: whereas the nuccal shelf (a curved shelf at the back of the skull) is only 1.50 cm thick

facts.statement: It coexisted with dinosaurs such as Pachyrhinosaurus, Edmontosaurus, and Nanuqsaurus, as well as the mammal Unnuakomys.
facts.quote: Alaskacephale coexisted with dinosaurs like the ceratopsian Pachyrhinosaurus, ornithopod Edmontosaurus, and tyrannosaurid Nanuqsaurus in addition to mammals like Unnuakomys

facts.statement: It lived at a paleolatitude of approximately 80 to 85 degrees North.
facts.quote: Having resided at an estimated 80°–85°N paleolatitude

facts.statement: Temperatures ranged from 10 to 12 degrees Celsius in summer and about -2 degrees Celsius in winter.
facts.quote: The temperature of this Northern environment would've ranged from around 10 to 12 °C during the warmer months and about −2 °C ± 3.9 °C during the colder months

facts.statement: The environment experienced 120 days of continuous low-light conditions during winter.
facts.quote: As well as this, the environment would have faced 120 days of continuous low-light conditions during the Winter

facts.statement: The lack of ectotherms suggests that animals thriving in this extreme latitude were endotherms.
facts.quote: Interestingly, due to the cooler conditions of this habitat, many otherwise common ectothermic clades lack representation entirely in the Prince Creek Formation, suggesting that all the animals that did thrive in these extreme latitudes were indeed endotherms to some degree

facts.statement: Sullivan argued that a specific suture was actually a breakage point, preventing it from uniting Alaskacephale and Pachycephalosaurus.
facts.quote: However, Sullivan opined that this "suture" is instead a breakage point in quadrates of both Alaskacephale and Pachycephalosaurus, so it could not be used to unite the two taxa

facts.statement: A 2023 study placed Alaskacephale as a sister taxon to Goyocephale, forming a clade with Homalocephale.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis in a 2023 study recovered Alaskacephale as a sister taxon of Goyocephale and the two genera formed a clade with Homalocephale

facts.statement: Alaskacephale lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 83 to 71 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 83 a 71 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: The genus was named by Robert Sullivan in 2006, referencing the state of Alaska where the fossil was discovered.

facts.statement: The species name honors paleontologist Roland Gangloff.
facts.quote: La especie fue nombrada en honor al paleontólogo Roland Gangloff

facts.quote: Este último medía 1,5 metros de largo y 10 kilogramos de peso

facts.quote: Alaskacephale se distingue de otros paquicefalosáuridos por la presencia de dos filas divergentes de nódulos óseos a lo largo del escamoso

facts.statement: Its arms were light and slender, ending in a hand with five fingers.

facts.statement: Alaskacephale was a member of the group Pachycephalosauria, a family of bipedal, herbivorous dinosaurs with thick skulls.
facts.quote: Alaskacephale era un miembro del grupo Pachycephalosauria, una familia de dinosaurios bípedos, herbívoros y de cráneo grueso

facts.statement: Currently, pachycephalosaurians are recognized as part of the larger group Marginocephalia, which includes them and gigantic horned ceratopsians.

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurini is the most advanced group within Pachycephalosauria and consists of North American members.
facts.quote: Pachycephalosaurini es el grupo más avanzado en Pachycephalosauria y está formado por miembros norteamericanos

facts.statement: Due to a lack of fossil remains, Alaskacephale is little known.
facts.quote: Alaskacephale, debido a la falta de restos fósiles, es poco conocido
